project.title: Front-of-House Guest Experience and Handover Upgrade
project.objective: Standardise and improve guest arrival, luggage handling, and issue escalation between porters and the contact centre to reduce complaints and wait times.
deliverables: Standardised guest arrival and departure workflow for porters and contact centre
Unified script for handling complaints and special needs requests
Luggage handling and room service support checklist
Escalation matrix between front-of-house and contact centre
Training huddles plan and quick-reference guide for staff
Simple tracking log for guest issues and resolutions
constraints: All changes must fit existing staffing levels and shift patterns
New procedures must comply with safety, hygiene, and security rules
No new software; use existing phones, radios, and basic office tools
Pilot must run during both weekday and weekend peak periods
Documentation must be simple enough for quick on-shift use

risks.risk: Porters do not consistently follow the new arrival and luggage workflow during busy periods.
risks.mitigation: Keep workflow to a one-page checklist, run short shift-start reminders, and spot-check usage in first two weeks.

risks.risk: Contact centre supervisors find the escalation matrix unclear and revert to old habits.
risks.mitigation: Co-create matrix with supervisors, test with sample calls, and adjust before full rollout.

risks.risk: New complaint handling script feels too rigid and impacts natural service style.
risks.mitigation: Include optional phrases and examples, gather feedback after first week, and refine wording.

risks.risk: Coordination between porters and contact centre breaks down during night shifts.
risks.mitigation: Add specific night-shift scenarios to procedures and assign a night-shift liaison to monitor issues.

themes.why_relevant: Core to porters’ work; needs to be predictable and smooth for guests and staff.
Both porters and contact centre face complaints; alignment reduces repeat issues.
Requires clear, safe handling and coordination across teams.
Any new process must respect existing safety, hygiene, and door security rules.
Good handovers avoid lost luggage, missed requests, and duplicated work.

backlog.task: Map current guest arrival and departure steps across porters and contact centre
definition_of_done: Current-state flow from guest arrival to departure documented in simple diagram
Pain points and delays identified with at least five concrete examples
Validated with at least two hotel porters from different shifts

backlog.task: Draft standard guest arrival and luggage handling checklist for porters
definition_of_done: Checklist covers greeting, luggage tagging, parking, and room delivery steps
Includes safety, hygiene, and door security checks
Reviewed and approved by contact centre supervisor and front office manager

backlog.task: Create unified complaint and escalation script for porters and contact centre
definition_of_done: Script includes opening, probing, resolution, and closing steps
Clear rules on when to escalate to supervisor or security
Tested in at least five role-play scenarios with porters

backlog.task: Design simple guest issue and resolution tracking log
definition_of_done: Log template created using existing office tools
Fields cover guest details, issue type, actions, and outcome
Pilot used for one week by both porters and contact centre and adjusted

backlog.task: Define coordination rules for special needs and vulnerable guests
definition_of_done: List of common special needs scenarios documented
Clear steps for porters and contact centre for each scenario
Security and housekeeping requirements included and validated

backlog.task: Create escalation matrix between porters, contact centre, and other teams
definition_of_done: Matrix lists typical issues and who to contact first and second
Includes day, evening, and night-shift variations
Shared in channel and printed for front desk and porter station

backlog.task: Plan and schedule short on-shift training huddles
definition_of_done: Huddle agenda created with key topics and timings
Schedule covers all shifts over a two-week period
Attendance tracking method agreed with front office manager

backlog.task: Pilot new workflows during weekend peak and collect feedback
definition_of_done: New checklist and scripts used for at least one full weekend
At least ten pieces of feedback collected from staff
Summary of issues and improvement ideas posted in channel

backlog.task: Align porter door security steps with new guest flow
definition_of_done: Security-sensitive steps identified in arrival and departure flow
Door security checks integrated into checklist without slowing service
Security officer confirms compliance with existing policies

backlog.task: Prepare quick-reference guide for front-of-house procedures
definition_of_done: Two-page max guide summarising key workflows and contacts
Language is simple and suitable for quick on-shift reading
Printed and placed at porter station and contact centre desks

backlog.task: Set up simple weekly review of complaints and incidents
definition_of_done: Recurring slot agreed with porters and supervisors
Template for reviewing top issues and actions created
First review completed and actions logged

backlog.task: Standardise handover notes between porter shifts
definition_of_done: Handover note template created for incoming shift
Includes open guest requests, luggage in storage, and incidents
Used for at least three consecutive handovers and refined

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on current guest journey and agree on main pain points to fix first.
threads_plan.trigger: contact centre supervisor posts draft of A1 and asks porters to validate and add missing steps.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on the final version of the current guest journey map in A1.
Select top three pain points to prioritise in the first rollout.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Co-create and finalise the porter arrival and luggage handling checklist.
threads_plan.trigger: hotel porter shares first proposal for A2 based on T2 and asks for feedback.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the steps and order in the porter checklist A2.
Decide how door security checks are integrated into A2 without slowing service.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Agree on complaint handling script and escalation matrix across teams.
threads_plan.trigger: contact centre supervisor posts draft A3 and A6 and requests comments from porters.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Confirm final wording and structure of the complaint script A3.
Approve escalation paths in A6 for day, evening, and night shifts.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Define approach for special needs guests and shift handovers before pilot.
threads_plan.trigger: hotel porter shares draft A5 and A8 and asks if they cover typical scenarios and handover needs.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on mandatory steps for handling special needs guests in A5.
Approve the standard handover template A8 and when it must be used.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Plan and review the weekend pilot and training huddles outcomes.
threads_plan.trigger: contact centre supervisor posts T7 and T8 plan and later shares pilot results for feedback.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Reconfirm that the pilot focuses on the previously agreed top pain points.
Reaffirm use of the approved complaint script during the pilot and beyond.

channel_rituals: Daily short async check-in at shift start to flag issues with new workflows.
End-of-week summary post reviewing complaints and key learnings.
Pre-weekend alignment message confirming pilot focus and any tweaks.
Post-incident debrief thread when a major guest issue occurs.
Monthly mini-review of checklists and guides to keep them current.
